summary: Specifies optional suites of algorithms and attributes that simplify the administration of IPsec, whether used with manual keying, IKEv1, or IKEv2. Since two IPsec systems must use the same algorithms to interoperate, preset suites reduce configuration. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Instead of picking every ingredient, you order a combo meal. These are ready-made combos of secret-keeping methods.

subtitle: Two named, ready-made bundles of IPsec algorithms so administrators do not have to pick each one.

tldr.problem: IPsec, IKE and IKEv2 offer so many algorithm choices that two systems are hard to make interoperate without careful pre-agreement.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two optional named suites, VPN-A and VPN-B, each fixing the encryption, integrity, pseudo-random function and Diffie-Hellman group, plus SA lifetimes for IKEv1.
tldr.outcome: Products that use the names VPN-A or VPN-B must match these values exactly. The RFC warns that some options may later turn out to be significantly weaker than believed.

today: RFC 4308 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its text describes itself as a companion to the IPsec architecture in RFC 2401, IKE and IKEv2 as they stood in December 2005.

sections.title: Why Named Suites Exist
sections.content:
IPsec, IKE and IKEv2 let users choose which cryptographic algorithms they use. Experience with IPsec in manual key mode and with IKE showed that there are so many choices for typical system administrators that interoperability is difficult without careful pre-agreement.

The IPsec Working Group therefore agreed that there should be a small number of named suites covering typical security policies. They are often called UI suites (user interface suites) because they may be shown in the administrative interface of an IPsec system. They are optional, and implementers may still allow individual selection of algorithms.

Although implementing the suites is optional, the document is on the standards track because anyone who calls a suite by one of these names has to conform to it. The suites are not extensions to IPsec, IKE or IKEv2. They are administrative methods for describing sets of configurations.
sections.eli5: There are so many settings that two people setting up a secret tunnel often pick different ones and cannot talk. A short list of named presets makes it easier to agree.

sections.title: Rules for Using the Suites
sections.content:
A UI suite is only a collection of values for some IPsec options. Using one does not change IPsec, IKE or IKEv2 in any way. The transform substructure in IKE and IKEv2 must still be used to carry the value of each option, whether or not suites are used.

Implementations that use UI suites SHOULD also offer a management interface for setting individual cryptographic options, because suites are unlikely to match everyone's security policy. They SHOULD use the names given here, SHOULD NOT use different names for these suites, and MUST NOT use these names for suites that do not match the listed values. These rules are needed for interoperability.

The suites here are meant for IPsec in virtual private networks. Other uses of IPsec will probably want to define their own suites with different names. More suites can be defined by later RFCs, and the name strings are registered by IANA.
sections.eli5: If you call your combo meal by a famous name, it has to contain exactly what that name promises. You can still offer a build-your-own menu too.

sections.title: The VPN-A and VPN-B Suites
sections.content:
VPN-A matches the commonly used corporate VPN security in IKEv1 at the time of publication. It uses the Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) with TripleDES in CBC mode for encryption and HMAC-SHA1-96 for integrity. For IKE and IKEv2 it uses TripleDES in CBC mode, HMAC-SHA1 as the pseudo-random function, HMAC-SHA1-96 for integrity and a 1024-bit MODP Diffie-Hellman group.

VPN-B is what many people expected corporate VPN security to look like within a few years of publication. ESP uses AES with 128-bit keys in CBC mode and AES-XCBC-MAC-96 for integrity. IKE and IKEv2 use AES-128 in CBC mode, AES-XCBC-PRF-128 as the pseudo-random function, AES-XCBC-MAC-96 for integrity and a 2048-bit MODP group.

In both suites, rekeying of Phase 2 (IKE) or the CREATE_CHILD_SA exchange (IKEv2) MUST be supported by both parties. The initiator MAY include a new Diffie-Hellman key. If it does, the key MUST be of the suite's group type (1024-bit MODP for VPN-A, 2048-bit MODP for VPN-B), and the responder MUST then include a Diffie-Hellman key of the same type.
sections.eli5: VPN-A is the older combo with older locks. VPN-B is the newer combo with stronger locks. Each one lists exactly which lock, which seal and which key-swap trick to use.

sections.title: Security Association Lifetimes for IKEv1
sections.content: IKEv1 has two security parameters that IKEv2 does not: the lifetime of the Phase 1 and the Phase 2 security associations (SAs). Systems that use IKEv1 with either VPN-A or VPN-B MUST use an SA lifetime of 86400 seconds (1 day) for Phase 1 and 28800 seconds (8 hours) for Phase 2.
sections.eli5: A secret handshake is only good for a while. The main one lasts one day and the smaller ones last eight hours, and then everyone must shake hands again.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document inherits all of the security considerations of the IPsec, IKE and IKEv2 documents. It adds one warning: some of the options in these suites may in the future be found to have properties significantly weaker than those believed at the time the document was produced.
sections.eli5: A lock that looks strong today might be picked tomorrow, so do not assume these presets stay safe forever.

sections.title: The IANA Registry of Suites
sections.content:
IANA created and maintains a registry called "Cryptographic Suites for IKEv1, IKEv2, and IPsec". Each entry is a text string and the number of the RFC that lists the associated transforms. New entries can be added only after RFC publication and approval by an expert designated by the IESG.

The initial values are VPN-A and VPN-B, both defined in RFC 4308.
sections.eli5: There is an official list of combo-meal names so that no two combos share a name.
